info.title: PACT — Programmable Agent Commerce Trust
info.summary: Contract-aware, fulfillment-gated PayPal settlement for agent-to-agent commerce.
info.description:
A buyer agent and a seller agent negotiate; PACT compiles a hashed contract, checks a deterministic spending policy, places a PayPal authorization, verifies the delivery and captures only if the contract is satisfied.

Rules that hold for every endpoint:

- The browser never supplies an amount, a status, a seller or a contract. Amounts come from the signed contract on the server.
- Identity is an anonymous session in a signed, http-only cookie. Only the session that created a deal may change it; showcase deals are read-only.
- State-changing requests must be same-origin and, where they have a body, JSON.
- Money is integer minor units (US cents). Timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC.
- Every response carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and an `x-request-id`.
- PACT runs against PayPal Sandbox only. Without credentials a simulator stands in and every payment is labelled `simulated`.

post.summary: Create a deal from a request in words
post.description: Derives the mandate, matches a seller agent and starts the negotiation. A request whose budget is stated only in a currency other than US dollars is refused (400): PACT settles in USD and does not guess a conversion. Creates the anonymous session if there is none. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked). Limits: 8 per session per 10 minutes, 40 per network address per hour.

get.description: Newest first. An empty list without a session; never creates one.
Readable by anyone holding the id (ids are unguessable; showcase deals are public). The buyer's private mandate is included only for the owning session.

200.description: The deal as the caller may see it.

post.summary: Execute at most one automatic step
post.description: Owner only. The deal's stored status decides which step runs; the caller cannot choose it. Runs under a per-deal lease: a concurrent call answers 200 with `busy: true`. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked).

200.description: The deal after the step, or unchanged when nothing ran.

post.summary: Record a human decision at a gate
post.description: Owner only. The decision must be one the deal's current gate offers (`next.options`), otherwise 409. The body never carries an amount or a status; a release still has to pass the settlement guard before any money moves. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked).

get.description: Seller-supplied content, served as an attachment under a sandboxing content security policy with MIME sniffing off.

post.summary: Compare PACT's ledger with the provider's record of the deal
post.description: Re-reads the order and authorization from the payment provider and compares them field by field with PACT's ledger. The verdict is deterministic. With PayPal Sandbox and AI enabled, a read-only auditor agent (PayPal Agent Toolkit, `get_order` only) adds a short statement; if it fails, the facts are returned alone. Changes no payment and no status. Anyone who can read the deal may call it; only the owner's call is written to the audit trail (`payment.reconciled`). State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked). Limits: 12 per session (or network address) per 10 minutes and, for callers with a session, 36 per network address per 10 minutes. The agent's statement is additionally budgeted for the whole deployment (120 per hour); beyond it the facts are returned alone.

200.description: The comparison. A provider failure is reported as `status: unavailable`, not as an error.

get.description: The calling session's deals plus the seeded showcase deals (newest first, at most 300), their payment events, verification checks and totals. Without a session only the showcase is returned. Read-only.
The default policy until one is saved. Never creates a session.

200.description: The policy and today's committed spend.

put.description: Applies to this session only and only to what happens next: a signed contract keeps the thresholds it was signed with. Creates the session if there is none. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked). Limits: 30 per session per 10 minutes, 120 per network address per hour.

get.description: Whether the session's wallet and the shared demo wallet are connected, and how the next in-policy deal will be approved. Never creates a session.

delete.description: Scope `session` forgets the caller's wallet (a no-op without a session). Scope `demo` forgets the shared wallet and requires the operator token. Existing authorizations are unaffected. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked).

post.description: Asks the provider for a vault setup token, stores it server-side as a pending connection and returns where the payer gives consent. Creates the session if there is none. Scope `demo` requires the operator token and binds the connection to the calling session. A connected wallet must be disconnected before another is connected (409). State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked). Limits: 10 per session per 10 minutes and 30 per network address per hour; 20 attempts on scope `demo` per network address per 10 minutes.

get.summary: What is configured in this deployment
get.description: Reports that integrations are configured, never their values. Answers 200 even when the database is unreachable; the affected components are then listed under `degraded`.

post.description: Called by PayPal, cross-origin and without a session. The signature is verified over the exact bytes of the body; an event that does not verify changes nothing. Verified events are de-duplicated on PayPal's event id and may only confirm or advance a payment along its state machine.

schema.description: A PayPal webhook event, at most 256 KiB.

200.description: Verified and applied, or needing no action.

400.description: Not verified, not a usable event, or too large. Empty body.

503.description: The deal is in the middle of a step; PayPal redelivers. Empty body.

get.summary: Return from the PayPal approval page
get.description: Browser redirect target. Nothing in the URL is trusted: the order authorized is the one stored for the deal, re-read from PayPal (status, amount, contract hash) before authorizing.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: PayPal's order id. Must equal the deal's stored order id.

Location.description: `/deals/{id}?paypal=approved|pending|error`, or `/workspace?paypal=error` for a malformed deal id.

get.summary: Return from a cancelled PayPal approval
get.description: Browser redirect target. Changes nothing: the deal keeps waiting for payment until its owner cancels it.

Browser redirect target. Exchanges the setup token stored for the pending connection — never a token from the URL — for the vault token and marks the wallet connected. For scope `demo` the returning browser must be the operator session that started the connection.

post.summary: Approve a simulated order as the payer
post.description: The simulated payer approves; PACT then authorizes exactly as after a real PayPal return. Exists only while the simulator stands in for PayPal: with PayPal Sandbox credentials configured it answers 404. Owner only. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked).

post.summary: Cancel a simulated order as the payer
post.description: The simulator voids the order and the deal is cancelled with it, recorded as the owner's decision. Exists only while the simulator stands in for PayPal: with PayPal Sandbox credentials configured it answers 404. Owner only. State-changing: must be same-origin (Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site are checked).

get.description: For a scheduler, not for browsers. Runs the next automatic step of deals that hold money (authorized, revision required, submitted, verified, rejecting) and have not changed for two minutes: verification and capture, or the release of a rejected delivery's hold, do not depend on the payer's browser staying open. One step per deal, a few deals per call, through the same lease and idempotency keys as `POST /api/deals/{id}/advance`. Never touches a deal before authorization or at a human gate.

examined.description: Stalled deals found for this run.

advanced.description: The deals a step was attempted for.

executed.description: The step that ran to completion, or null when it stalled (the deal's `lastError` says why).

get.summary: Whether the dashboard agents can run here
get.description: Reports whether the Operations dashboard's AI agents are available on this deployment and which models they may use. Starts no session and calls no model.

message.description: One sentence for the visitor when `available` is false.

post.summary: Model proxy for the dashboard agents
post.description: Accepts an OpenAI Responses-format request from the Operations dashboard, rebuilds it from an allow-list of fields and forwards it to the AI Gateway with PACT's own credentials. Only the allowed models are ever called, output is capped, and the caller is rate-limited per session and per network address. The provider's answer (JSON, or a server-sent event stream when `stream` is true) is passed straight back. May start a session.

schema.description: An OpenAI Responses-format request. Fields outside the allow-list are dropped.

session.name: pact_sid
session.description: Anonymous session: `<id>.<HMAC-SHA256>`; http-only, SameSite=Lax. Set by the endpoints that may start a session.

adminToken.name: x-admin-token
adminToken.description: Operator token for the shared demo wallet. Compared in constant time; rejected when none is configured.

cronSecret.description: The deployment's CRON_SECRET, sent by the scheduler as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` (what Vercel Cron does). Compared in constant time; the endpoint answers 404 while no secret is configured.

InvalidRequest.description: The request is malformed: not JSON, too large, or failing validation (`invalid_request`).

Forbidden.description: Cross-site request, missing session, not the deal's owner, or missing operator token (`forbidden`).

Conflict.description: The action is not possible in the current state (`conflict`).

RateLimited.description: Too many requests (`rate_limited`); `details.resetAt` says when the window ends and `Retry-After` how many seconds that is from now.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the rate-limit window reopens.

PaymentError.description: The payment provider could not complete the step (`payment_error`); `details` carries the provider's issue code and debug id.

Internal.description: Unexpected failure (`internal`). Details are logged under the request id, never returned.

Unavailable.description: A dependency this request needs is switched off or did not answer (`unavailable`).

Minor.description: Money in integer minor units (US cents). Never a float.

Category.description: Kind of work. `other` has no seller; `restricted` is always blocked by policy.

DealStatus.description: Deal lifecycle state. Transitions are table-driven; the last eight values are terminal.

PaymentStatus.description: Payment lifecycle state: none → created → approved → authorized → captured | voided | expired | failed.

ProviderKind.description: `simulated` is the labelled stand-in used only when no PayPal Sandbox credentials are configured.

ApprovalMode.description: How the payer consented: in PayPal for this order, or once through a delegated (vaulted) agent wallet.

StepKind.description: An automatic step of the engine. One call to /advance executes at most one.

Mandate.description: The buyer's private instruction derived from the request. Only returned to the session that owns the deal.

GuardrailNote.description: A correction the deterministic rules engine made to an agent's proposal.

Contract.description: The immutable contract compiled from the agreed terms.

termsHash.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of `contract`. Written to the PayPal order as custom_id `pact:v1:<hash>`.

Policy.description: Deterministic spending policy. autonomousLimitMinor ≤ maxTransactionMinor and humanReviewMinConfidence ≤ autoCaptureMinConfidence.

aspectRatio.description: Aspect ratio the seller claims; the verifier recomputes it.

degraded.description: True when the AI evaluator was unavailable and AI rules were marked uncertain.

hash.description: sha256(prevHash + canonical JSON of the event).

AuditEvent.description: One entry of the hash-chained audit trail.

demoFault.description: Set only for sellers with a controlled demo fault.

approveUrl.description: Where the payer approves the order. A path for the simulator.

PaymentRecord.description: The deal's payment as PACT records it. All ids are the provider's. Never contains a vault id.

NextStep.description: What happens next: an automatic step, a human gate, or nothing.

isOwner.description: True when the calling session created this deal and may act on it.

contract.description: The hashed contract plus the live payment state (the state is not part of the hash).

auditChainValid.description: Result of re-verifying the audit hash chain on read.

intent.description: The request in plain words, 10–600 characters after cleaning. May be empty when scenarioId is given.

scenarioId.description: Optional demo scenario: pre-fills the request and pins the seller agent — as long as the request still asks for the kind of work that seller offers; otherwise the request is matched like a free-form one.

tzOffsetMinutes.description: The browser's Date#getTimezoneOffset(), so "tomorrow at 6 PM" resolves in local time.

CreateDealRequest.description: No amount, status, seller or contract can be supplied: they are derived on the server.

busy.description: True when another request holds the step lease; poll again.

percent.description: Required for release_partial: percentage of the contract price to capture.

origin.description: `mine` = created by the calling session, `showcase` = seeded reference deals.

heldMinor.description: Authorized and neither captured nor released.

hoursToDeadline.description: One decimal; negative once the deadline has passed.

day.description: UTC day the deal was created.

OpsRow.description: One row of the operations ledger.

type.description: The audit event type without its `payment.` prefix.

amountMinor.description: The amount the event itself states; 0 when it states none.

reference.description: The most specific provider id the event is about.

releasedMinor.description: Voided or expired authorizations plus the uncaptured remainder of partial captures.

pendingHumanReview.description: Deals waiting for a spend approval or a delivery review.

verificationFailureRate.description: Share of first deliveries that were not capture-eligible. 0 when nothing was verified.

firstPassRate.description: Share of first deliveries that were capture-eligible. 0 when nothing was verified.

webhooks.description: A webhook id for signature verification is configured.

delegatedWallet.description: The shared demo wallet is connected, so in-policy deals authorize without a PayPal login.

degraded.description: Present only when a component could not be checked or is misconfigured.

SystemStatus.description: What is configured, never the values.

WalletScope.description: `session` = the caller's own wallet; `demo` = the shared wallet of the public demo (operator only).

WalletStatus.description: Delegated agent wallet status. The vault id is never part of any response.

approveUrl.description: Absolute URL where the payer gives consent.

pact.description: PACT's ledger value. For statuses it includes what PACT expects the provider to report.

status.description: Computed deterministically from `facts`. `unavailable`: there was nothing to compare or the provider could not be read.

narrative.description: Plain-language statement by the read-only auditor agent. Null when the agent did not run.

toolCalls.description: PayPal Agent Toolkit tools the agent called, in order. Only `get_order` is ever available to it.

details.description: Present for some errors: validation issues, `{ resetAt }` for rate limits, `{ issue, debugId, retryable }` for payment errors.

ApiErrorBody.description: Every error response has this shape. Internal details are logged with the request id, never returned.
